summary: Both hypotheses confirmed. The enhanced algorithm (perturbed MST restarts + relay reassignment + degree-3 hub insertion) scored 87.162/100, improving +0.211 over the iter-1 baseline of 86.951. The ablation arm scored 87.033, confirming both components contribute independently.
key_points: h-main CONFIRMED: Score 87.162 vs predicted ≥87.05, a +0.211 improvement over iter-1 baseline (86.951). Matches the designer's probe measurement exactly.

h-ablation CONFIRMED: Restarts-only scored 87.033, correctly ordering as baseline (86.951) < ablation (87.033) < full algorithm (87.162). This cleanly decomposes the gain: perturbed restarts contribute ~0.082 pts (39%), relay reassignment + hub insertion contribute ~0.129 pts (61%).

Surprise: Post-processing steps (relay reassignment + degree-3 hub insertion) contribute more than perturbed restarts alone, contrary to the designer's initial expectation that restarts were the primary driver.

Stability concern: Under CPU contention, the time-limited perturbation loop produces fewer trials, causing occasional score regression to ~77 (likely one test case hitting the 10s time limit). Stable 87.162 requires uncontended CPU.
Remaining gap: ~1.3 points of potential improvement remain, concentrated in tests 3, 5, 8, and 10. Tests 1 and 2 are structurally limited by having only K=10 relay stations available.
